expects.rule: Content is organised around four distinct needs: tutorials (learning), how-to guides (a task), reference (facts) and explanation (concepts), and each page serves one of them.
Pages are written in second person, active voice, with sentence-case headings and link text that says where the link goes.
Pages are short and scannable: users read about 20% of the words on an average page, so put the answer and the next step first and cut the rest.
Search is reachable from every page, with a keyboard shortcut (Ctrl or Cmd+K), and a persistent side navigation shows where the page sits.
Code samples can be copied in one click, name the language, and let the reader switch language or framework when several apply.
Every page shows its last update date and offers a way to report an error or edit the page.
A getting-started path leads a new reader to a first working result in a few steps, from the home page.
Body text keeps a line length of 50 to 75 characters and works in light and dark themes.

traits: A left tree, a content column and an on-page list sit side by side on 3 of 8 first screens (Kubernetes, Next.js, Tailscale); Vercel has the tree only; Stripe, Docker, Netlify and Vue open on a landing grid or hero.
A search field or search button is on the first screen on 8 of 8; a keyboard hint (/, Ctrl K, command K) is shown on 4 of 8 (Stripe, Vue, Next.js, Vercel).
One sans-serif family for text on 8 of 8 (Inter, Geist, Open Sans, Roboto Flex, Instrument Sans) with a mono face for code.
The docs home is an index of entry points on 5 of 8 (Stripe, Docker, Netlify, Kubernetes, Vercel); Vue opens on a hero with four buttons.
A copyable code block or command is on the first screen on 2 of 8 (Stripe, Vercel).
Page title of 32 to 56px on 7 of 8 sites; Vue's marketing headline is 76px.
An AI helper in the first screen on 5 of 8 (Stripe, Docker, Next.js, Vercel, Netlify; Tailscale offers Copy as Markdown instead).
Feedback or edit controls are visible on the first screen on 2 of 8 (Next.js, Kubernetes); a last-validated date on 1 (Tailscale).

sites.name: Stripe Docs
sites.why: Pale blue header band with a search field showing a / shortcut, an Ask AI button and a product tab row; a 32px Documentation title with a dotted pattern, a blue Get started button, three columns of task links (Payments, Revenue, Developers), then a Try it out panel with a dark copyable CLI snippet. System sans-serif text and a mono face for code.
sites.recognition: Listed first in draft.dev '12 Documentation Examples Every Developer Tool Can Learn From', updated 2025-09-05

sites.name: Kubernetes Documentation
sites.why: Blue header with a version menu and a theme switch, an event notice, then a three-column page: collapsible tree on the left (Getting started, Concepts, Tasks, Tutorials, Reference), breadcrumb and a two-column grid of grey topic cards in the middle, Create an issue on the right. All in Open Sans.

sites.name: Docker Docs
sites.why: Bright blue header with four links, a Gordon AI button and Search, a 40px 'How can we help?' title over a large ask-anything input, five example questions as pills, then four cards (Get started, Guides, Manuals, Reference) with one line each. Roboto Flex, light grey (#f9fafb) page.

sites.name: Vue.js
sites.why: White page, search with a Ctrl K hint, header links Docs, Playground, Ecosystem, About, Support with theme and social icons, a 76px two-line headline with 'Progressive' in a green-to-blue gradient, four buttons (Why Vue, Get Started, Install, a security-updates link), then three feature columns. Inter.

sites.name: Next.js Docs
sites.why: Off-white page (#fafafa) in Geist Sans, a 40px title, a Copy page button, left sidebar with a router switch and a version selector, long-form text with 'How to use the docs', and a right column of on-page links plus Give feedback and Edit this page on GitHub. Search shows a command-K hint.

sites.name: Vercel Docs
sites.why: Off-white page, a sidebar with a search field and a command-K hint, a 56px headline 'Ship anything with Vercel', three buttons, a tabbed terminal block with a copy button (npm i -g vercel, login), and below an Agent Prompt box. Sidebar groups: Start, Build AI apps, Run agents and backends.

sites.name: Netlify Docs
sites.why: White page with a nine-item header including AI, a blue announcement bar, a 48px title, three cards (Create a new project, Build with AI, Start with a framework), a teal deploy button and an outlined Set up domain, and a mono WHAT'S NEW label. Ask Netlify button bottom right.

sites.name: Tailscale Docs
sites.why: Quickstart page under the marketing header: sidebar tree, search field, breadcrumb, a 36px title, 'Last validated: Jan 5, 2026' with Copy as Markdown and View as Markdown links, a welcome sentence and an embedded video, and an On this page list at right. Privacy banner at the bottom.

avoid: A marketing hero with a large illustration and slogan on the docs home, pushing the entry points below the first screen.
Documentation as one long page or a PDF, with no search, no side navigation and no anchors for headings.
Mixing tutorial, task steps, reference and explanation in the same page, so no reader finds the one thing they came for.
Code shown as an image, or without a copy button and language label.
Dead-end pages: no last update date, no next step, no way to report a mistake.
Low-contrast grey body text and small type to look 'clean', hard to read in dark mode.
Search that only matches exact titles, or that is hidden behind a menu on phones.
